chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Faddal, from Dawud ibn Farqad, from Abu al-Hasan Zakariyya ibn Yahya, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Whatever God has concealed from the servants, it is removed from their accountability.

key_terms.الْعِبَادُ: The servants (of God), humankind — emphasizing the relationship of dependency and accountability
key_terms.حَجَبَ: To veil, conceal, screen off — used in jurisprudence for knowledge withheld by God from human access
key_terms.مَوْضُوعٌ: Set aside, removed, lifted — a jurisprudential term indicating the removal or suspension of an obligation

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Sadiq say about accountability for things God has concealed?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) articulates a foundational principle of Shia jurisprudence and theology: divine concealment entails human exemption from accountability. In the context of the chapter on the 'Proof of God upon His creatures' (al-hujja), this hadith addresses the question of what obligations God places on people — the answer being that any matter God has hidden or made inaccessible is not a binding obligation. The early Shia community would have understood this as a safeguard against legal rigorism: one cannot be held responsible for what lies beyond the bounds of accessible knowledge.
